messages:
jules: Quick heads-up — long-context load test (seq=128k, multi-shard) shows steady memory growth in the KV cache plus high fragmentation over time. pprof shows a lot of small free runs, not being coalesced.
perf-bot: Perf alert: kv-cache.memory_growth +28% over baseline during run at 1975002400 — regression flagged.
maria: Can you paste the top allocations / profiles? rough numbers are fine.
jules: Sure — top stats: inuse_space ~ 1.2GB -> 1.9GB over 6h; frag ratio ~ 52%. Many ~4–32KB free blocks between large used segments.
seth: Sounds like our free-list/coalescing path isn't triggering for these sizes. Which allocator flags were used? buddy vs segregated?
jules: We're on the quick-alloc (segregated) path; coalesce disabled in hot path to avoid stalls. The regression correlates to the change that disabled background compaction in commit c3a7d2f.
elaine: Proposal idea: bucket-reflow compaction — periodic background pass that compacts small holes into contiguous pages and updates shard pointers. Not full GC (too expensive), but bounded window reclamation.
chao: +1 for bounded compaction. We should also try changing block granularity. In current config: --kv.block_size=65536, maybe try 32768 or 16384 for workloads with many short-lived tokens.
maria: Would smaller block sizes increase alloc overhead? trade-off math?
seth: Yes, smaller blocks reduce internal fragmentation but increase metadata overhead & pointer traffic. Our perf model says switching 64KB -> 16KB could reduce observed fragmentation from 52% -> ~18% on synthetic short-chunk traces, CPU overhead ~+6% for allocator ops. Worth testing.
jules: I ran a quick A/B with 32KB: fragmentation dropped to ~30%, mem growth plateaued earlier. CPU delta small on that run. Logs: 
```
# run summary
kv-shard-3: start mem 1.1GB -> 1.45GB (32KB blocks)
kv-shard-3: baseline (64KB) had 1.1GB -> 1.9GB
p99 latency unchanged
```
elaine: Good data. For the compaction proto I sketched: periodic per-shard sweeper with these properties — max work per second, non-blocking handoff, and a 'chunk-coalescer' that only touches free ranges adjacent to >=2 free neighbors. If compaction hits >X ms for a pass, back off.
chao: Also consider adaptive block sizing: new allocations pick block class based on recent allocation size histogram (like tcmalloc central cache idea). That could reduce churn without global config changes.
maria: Any risk to current running Dedicated customers if we flip block_size? rollout plan?
seth: Staged rollout: feature flag controlled, per-tenant override, start with dev/staging -> canary (5%) -> 25% -> 100%. Need telemetry: frag ratio, mem_growth curve, alloc ops/s, tail latency.
jules: I'll open a short RFC with the experiment plan + perf run configs and the pprof dump. TL;DR: try 32KB immediate canary + background bounded bucket-reflow compaction proto.
elaine: I'll add the compaction prototype patch (non-default) and a small microbenchmark for coalescing cost.
perf-bot: Noted: created perf run request #PR-4621 for canary +32KB + compaction=false; #PR-4622 for +32KB + compaction=true.
maria: Awesome. One more ask — add a small regression test that simulates long-context token churn so CI can catch this before release.
jules: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
